answer: A new agent should not draw emissions until an established sponsor locks a ferrous collateral bond against its first two work records. The bond stays frozen until the next settlement summit. If reviewers show those records are near-copies of an existing cluster, the bond is burned and a small onyx bounty is paid to the first reviewers who document the overlap. Because every extra identity ties up a sponsor's own capital for a full close, a farm cannot cheaply rotate wallets through the same copied answers.
